$comment: Read-time petrification contract, shared by the Go backend and every frontend. The line is min(now − horizon, midnight today) and phase is a pure function of (block span, now, line) — no table, no job, nothing to migrate. Both sides run these scenarios as a test table; a divergence is a test failure, not a production surprise.

boundaries.$comment: Copied from the prototype's comparison operators. These decide the edges and are the first thing to check when two implementations disagree.
boundaries.stone: end <  line   (a block ending exactly ON the line is NOT stone)
boundaries.recon: end <= now    (a block ending exactly NOW is recon)
boundaries.now: start <= now  (a block starting exactly NOW is now)

scenarios.name: timezone — the same instant classifies differently for viewers in different zones
scenarios.$comment: The same instant is 2am on the 26th in Shanghai but 2pm on the 25th in New York — so the viewer's zone decides both which day is 'today' and which half of the min() wins. Here it is still mid-afternoon locally, so rolling (09:00) is later than midnight and midnight wins; a Shanghai viewer at the same instant is past midnight and gets the rolling line instead.

still today in New York, so still editable

still afternoon in New York

dst.$comment: Measured against Go's time.ParseInLocation, not reasoned about — the standard library documents the gap case as 'not guaranteed', so the observed behaviour IS the contract. A frontend that resolves these differently will disagree with the server about whether a block has frozen.

springForward.note: 02:00→03:00; wall clocks in [02:00, 03:00) never happen. Go resolves them BACKWARDS, to one hour before the nominal reading.

fallBack.note: 01:00→01:00; the hour repeats. Go picks the FIRST (pre-transition, EDT) occurrence.

startOfDay.why: the transition is at 02:00, so midnight itself is unaffected
same — midnight is before the 01:00 transition

midnightGap.$comment: The class the America/New_York cases above cannot reach, and the reason those cases read as reassuring: they say midnight is unaffected BECAUSE the transition is at 02:00. Some zones shift AT 00:00, and there the local day does not begin at midnight at all. Go folds a wall-clock reading that never happened BACKWARDS, so the obvious time.Date(y,m,d,0,0,0,0,loc) returns 23:00 on the PREVIOUS day — a start-of-day outside its own day. Measured against Go's tzdata. A client that computes midnight naively will disagree with the server about what has frozen and about when a card dies; before this was fixed, an ask-first card created after 23:00 on one of these dates was born already expired.

cases.note: clocks jump 00:00 → 01:00, so the day begins at 01:00
control — the shift is at 02:00, so midnight exists and nothing moves

invariants: startOfDay(t) falls on the same calendar date as t
